headline: Anthropic has reportedly agreed a multiyear deal to buy cloud computing services from IREN, a data-centre company that used to mine bitcoin.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: a single unconfirmed report, relayed by one short article, with no value, size or start date given.
importance_line: Another large computing supplier would help Anthropic secure the chips and power its AI products need, but neither company has confirmed the deal, no value or start date is reported, and the link to IREN's earlier unnamed customer is only believed.
summary: The Information reports (as relayed by Crypto Briefing) that Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, has signed a multiyear cloud-services agreement with IREN, a data-centre operator formerly involved in bitcoin mining; neither company has confirmed it. IREN had earlier mentioned a contract with an unnamed customer it called a "leading frontier AI lab" (a developer of cutting-edge AI models), now believed to be Anthropic, which would add IREN to Anthropic's computing suppliers alongside Amazon Web Services and Google as it expands its data centres.
notes: The Information original was not opened; text read on Crypto Briefing, which credits it, so the url is the Crypto Briefing page. The Crypto Briefing text is short and gives no terms. A TradingKey analysis piece said the partner was 'confirmed'; this entry keeps the more cautious Crypto Briefing wording that neither company has confirmed.
